Definition: to pierce; to be hollow, or (figuratively) foolish
BiblicalUsage: Nabab means to pierce or to be hollow, and its four occurrences are mostly about things made hollow. In Exodus 27:8 the altar is to be made hollow with boards, as it was shown to Moses on the mount, and in Jeremiah 52:21 the bronze pillars of the temple are described as hollow, four fingers thick.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a hollow altar still holds the fire, and that is the point; God does not need solid bronze to receive a sacrifice; He needs a people who build it the way He showed them.
